items.title: Confusion Over What Peel Region Actually Does Prompts New 24/7 Virtual Assistant Tool
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region launched a new online virtual assistant on August 31 to help residents of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon navigate the wide range of services the region provides. The outlet reports Peel Region handles services many people don't realize fall under its umbrella, including public health, paramedics, affordable housing, water, waste management, social services and transportation programs. INsauga reports the assistant is available around the clock in more than 30 languages, including English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese. According to the outlet, the tool can also walk visitors through creating a My Account profile, which gives access to services such as the Affordable Transit Program, Peel Living housing services and water bill payments. INsauga reports the launch is part of a broader push by the region to modernize its digital services and cut down on the long-standing confusion among residents about exactly what Peel Region does.

items.title: Exchange District's Growing Food Lineup Adds a Mystery Sushi and Sake Concept From a Toronto Team
items.summary: According to INsauga, a Toronto restaurant team is preparing to open a Japanese Fish Market sushi and sake bar inside Mississauga's Exchange District, a mixed residential and retail development in the works downtown. The outlet reports the project will include more than two million square feet of retail, dining, office and commercial space, along with resident amenities like a gym, yoga room, pet spa, meditation lounge and rooftop pool. INsauga reports other confirmed food concepts for the development include Toronto's Zaza Espresso Bar, Mediterranean restaurant Byblos, a steakhouse, a speakeasy and a new cafe concept from Tim Hortons. According to the outlet, Japanese Fish Market has so far only teased the opening through social media graphics branded Sushi and Sake Bar and Next Stop Sushi and Sake, with a look inspired by a traditional Japanese fish market. INsauga reports no firm opening date has been announced yet for the new concept.

items.title: Renamed Ternopil Park Cements Mississauga's Sister-City Bond With Ukrainian Community
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's Gulleden Park, next to the Burnhamthorpe Community Centre, has been renamed Ternopil Park to reflect the city's sister-city partnership with Ternopil, a city of roughly 225,000 people in western Ukraine. The outlet reports the twinning agreement was struck in May, after city council approved establishing the relationship on April 29 and the two cities' mayors signed official documents on May 15. INsauga reports the renaming was unanimously approved by council in July and follows a motion from Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca that cited Mississauga's growing and active Ukrainian community. According to the outlet, city planning and building commissioner Andrew Whittemore said in a report to the Heritage Advisory Committee that the new name shows Mississauga wants to engage with the world, and the renaming has so far drawn no public objections. INsauga reports Gulleden Park reopened on June 20 with a number of new amenities and upgrades before taking on its new name, and Mississauga's sister-city pact with Ternopil follows similar agreements between 16 other Canadian and Ukrainian cities.

items.title: Mississauga Police Shooting That Killed 19-Year-Old Kaleym Davy Prompts Family March and Fundraising Push
items.summary: According to NOW Toronto, the family of 19-year-old Kaleym Davy is organizing a memorial march this coming weekend after he was shot and killed during an interaction with Toronto police on Delfi Road in Mississauga on August 6. The outlet reports Davy's aunt shared details of the march in a social media post, with the family asking anyone who wants to attend to contact organizers directly for the location rather than publicizing it widely. NOW Toronto reports the march comes as Davy's family continues to press for answers about the circumstances of his death and considers pursuing legal action and representation. According to the outlet, the family has also launched a GoFundMe campaign with a public goal of $45,000, while family members say their overall target is $100,000. NOW Toronto reports the funds raised are intended to cover funeral and burial costs along with legal fees, with the campaign describing the family's goal as giving Davy a proper farewell while helping them find answers and pursue justice.

items.title: Two-and-a-Half-Year Wait for Autism Program Leaves Mississauga Grade 2 Student Without Support
items.summary: According to INsauga, a Mississauga mother says her twin daughters, both diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, are struggling to get the support they need as they head into Grade 2 at St. Charles Garnier Catholic Elementary School. The outlet reports Roselynn Desousa said her daughter Ava, who also has hearing loss, has fallen behind despite the family trying multiple approaches, including an Applied Behaviour Analysis program that did not work even after switching instructors. INsauga reports Desousa and her husband Antonio have met with school officials and have been on the waiting list for the Ontario Autism Program for two and a half years. According to the outlet, a school educational assessment found that Ava needs a dedicated educational assistant, but the school board says it lacks the funding to provide one. INsauga reports Ontario's Ministry of Education did not respond to requests for an interview, and the local school trustee referred questions back to the ministry.

items.title: Mississauga Staff Recommend Approval of Scaled-Back Lakeshore Road Condo Despite 2,000-Signature Petition
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city staff are recommending approval of the revised condo proposal at 900 Lakeshore Road West near Whittier Crescent, despite two petitions against the project gathering more than 2,000 signatures. The outlet reports an August 19 staff report calls for amending the official plan and zoning bylaw to allow the development to proceed. Mississauga.com reports the applicant made a resubmission on March 26, 2026, cutting the building's height from 10 storeys to nine and reducing the number of units from 188 to 161. According to the outlet, the revised plan also increases residential parking to one space per unit and includes an agreement to dedicate the portions of the property containing natural heritage features to the city. Mississauga.com reports the staff recommendation goes before Mississauga's Planning and Development Committee on September 8.

items.title: Mississauga's New Rental Licensing Bylaw Aims to Curb Renoviction-Driven Evictions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's new Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw took effect Tuesday, aiming to stop landlords from using major repair or renovation claims as a pretext to push out tenants, a practice known as renovictions. The outlet reports city council adopted the bylaw in April after developing it with input from tenants, landlords and community groups across Mississauga. INsauga reports the rules work alongside Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act and are meant to make the eviction process clearer and fairer while reducing housing instability. According to the outlet, city officials said the changes are also intended to help protect Mississauga's supply of affordable rental housing. INsauga reports the bylaw comes after renovictions became increasingly common in the city in recent years, prompting municipal politicians to respond.

items.title: Replica of Canada's Legendary Avro Arrow Finds a Permanent Home Back in Malton
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a full replica of the legendary Avro Arrow has returned to Malton, the community where the aircraft was originally designed and built nearly 69 years ago. The city reports the replica now stands in the new Flight Garden at Paul Coffey Park, the culmination of years of work by Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart, the city, the Malton Business Improvement Area and a group of donors. According to the city, the first CF-105 Avro Arrow rolled out of Avro Canada's Malton facilities in 1957 and remains one of the country's most celebrated aerospace engineering achievements. The city says the aircraft's legacy helped establish Malton as a hub for aerospace manufacturing, an industry that has grown into Canada's largest aerospace and aviation cluster, with more than 330 companies and over 32,000 employees based in Mississauga today. According to the city, that sector has grown by nearly 50 per cent over the past decade, reinforcing Mississauga's position as a leader in advanced manufacturing and aviation technology.

items.title: Scaled-Down Lorne Park Condo Proposal Heads to Council After Years of Resident Pushback
items.summary: According to INsauga, a scaled-down condominium proposal for 900 Lakeshore Road West in Lorne Park is heading back to city hall after years of neighbourhood opposition. The outlet reports the site sits beside Richard's Memorial Park and is currently home to a single detached house with a pool. INsauga reports the project was first pitched in 2023 as an 11-storey building with 178 units, revised in 2025 to 10 storeys and 188 units, and has now been reduced again to nine storeys with 161 units. According to the outlet, some residents have dubbed the development a cruise ship because of its bulk, and the 900 Lakeshore Committee has raised concerns over wind effects, damage to the site's Carolinian forest, added traffic, parking overflow onto parkland and groundwater management. INsauga reports the latest version goes before Mississauga's Planning and Development Committee on September 8, with a city report noting the developer would also transfer wooded portions of the property to the city.

items.title: Four Comedians Bring Nostalgia-Fuelled Gen X Humour to the Living Arts Centre This October
items.summary: According to Exclaim!, the City of Mississauga and saugaLIVE are bringing a lineup of Gen X comedians to the Living Arts Centre on October 9 for the GenX Takeover Comedy Tour. The outlet reports the night is billed as a mix of laughter, nostalgia and jokes about getting older, aimed squarely at audiences who grew up in the Gen X era. Exclaim! reports the bill features Real Slim Sherri, Kelly Manno, Dadbod Veteran (Jon Willington), Professor Nick Harrison and Justin Rupple. According to the outlet, tickets are already on sale, and fans can upgrade to a VIP package that includes a post-show meet and greet, a photo opportunity, an autographed poster and swag. Exclaim! reports a buffet dinner add-on will also be available before the show at LIVE Restaurant, located steps from the theatre, with organizers recommending reservations even though walk-ins are accepted.
